findings.title: .gitattributes byte-exactness rules do not cover patches/**; future Windows checkout could break the recorded SHA256 chain
findings.detail: The RCA repo has core.autocrlf=true and .gitattributes '* text=auto' with explicit '-text' (no-conversion) overrides for evidence/raw/** and evidence/phase2/** only. patches/phase5_1/canonical/*.patch are currently UNTRACKED, and tracked patches/phase5/canonical/*.patch blobs were verified byte-identical to the working tree (stored 76fd6623/d37376c9/59306105 == working bytes), so there is NO current corruption. However, if the phase5_1 patches are committed under the current attributes, a fresh clone/checkout on Windows would smudge the patch files to CRLF in the working tree, and their SHA256 would no longer match the values recorded in FINAL_HANDOFF.json / freeze evidence.
findings.resolution: Before committing patches/phase5_1 (and ideally for all patches/**), add a 'patches/** -text' rule to .gitattributes. Re-verify the three sha256 values from a fresh checkout afterwards.

findings.title: git format-patch --stdout reproduction differs from the series concat by exactly 2 bytes
findings.detail: format-patch --stdout for the 3-commit range hashes to 85434328... (50623 bytes) vs the canonical concat 797a69b5... (50621 bytes); byte-level cmp shows stdout inserts one extra 0x0A after patch 1 and after patch 2 (at bytes 15547 and 23e... offsets, i.e. between signature and next 'From '). Per-file regeneration with 'git format-patch -o <dir>' reproduces all three canonical files BYTE-IDENTICALLY (14719b8b/7d40c314/3eb20ec0), so the manifest's sha256_file_concat_v1 over the three files is unambiguous and correct. Risk is only that a future reproducer using --stdout gets a confusing mismatch.
findings.resolution: In reproduction instructions (e.g. the freeze doc), state that regeneration must use per-file output (-o / one file per commit), not --stdout, and that the series hash is over the concatenation of the three files with no separator.

findings.title: patches/phase5_1/canonical/ lacks the README.md present in the phase3/phase4/phase5 canonical dirs
findings.detail: patches/phase5/canonical/ and patches/phase4/canonical/ each contain a README.md; patches/phase5_1/ contains only canonical/ with the three .patch files and no README. No integrity impact; the manifest records all identities.
findings.resolution: Optionally add a short README.md pointing to findings/phase5_1/FINAL_HANDOFF.json for the hash manifest, mirroring earlier phases.

findings.title: RCA repo phase5_1 artifacts are untracked (not yet committed)
findings.detail: git status in the RCA repo shows patches/phase5_1/, findings/phase5_1/, docs/phase5_1/, evidence/phase5_1/, scripts/phase5_1/ as untracked, plus modified docs/phase5 (4 files) and findings/phase5 (1 file). The modified phase5 files are annotated supersession corrections whose new hash values I independently verified against the immutable patch bytes; nothing under patches/phase3, patches/phase4, findings/phase3, findings/phase4, docs/phase3, docs/phase4 is modified. Until committed, the evidence chain lives only in the working tree.
findings.resolution: Commit the phase5_1 artifacts (after applying finding A-1's .gitattributes rule) so the frozen evidence is protected by the RCA repo's history.

checks.name: DCO: no Signed-off-by anywhere; PENDING marker on all three commits
